meta.title: WrestlePower e-fed universe (PCW, WPW, EWE, POWER CW), 2005-2013
meta.description: Characters, championships, events, stables, feuds and storylines from the wrestlepower.net e-wrestling federations, rebuilt from the Wayback Machine and the e-wrestling fan wiki.
meta.schema_guide: See README.md next to this file.

promotions.name: Professional Championship Wrestling (PCW)
promotions.summary: The fed WPW grew out of. Run by The Judge on the Innovators of Wrestling (IOW) forums, it was absorbed by WPW after losing the interpromotional war at When Worlds Collide.
promotions.history:
PCW was a storyline-driven e-fed hosted on iowrestling.net, the Innovators of Wrestling forums, which had close ties to WrestlePower. The Judge was a former owner. Many of the people who later built WPW started here, and several of WPW's titles began life as PCW belts: the God of Live title, the Hardcore title and the IOW Championship.

PCW crowned champions such as The Dream (two-time PCW World Champion), The Killing Joke and, from 12 December 2006, "Unstoppable" Mike Adams. It ran the first two Tournament of Champions events; WPW's ToC III in 2008 continued the numbering.

In late 2006 PCW and WPW went to war on screen. PCW talent invaded Whiplash and Tuesday Night Turmoil, WPW wrestlers such as Mike Corral and Dan Murph defected, and the feud was settled at When Worlds Collide on 3 January 2007, a joint PPV with role-play threads posted on both forums. WPW won the main event five-on-five, PCW closed, and WPW took over its contracts. The PCW World title survived until The One unified it with the WPW title at Redemption on 13 May 2007.

WPW honoured PCW with a place in its 2008 Hall of Fame as "the company in which WPW grew from". A PCW Reunion Show card was posted for 4 July 2009 (t16003, not recovered).

promotions.name: WrestlePower Wrestling (WPW)
promotions.summary: The flagship fed of wrestlepower.net. Role-play based: the better RP won. Weekly Tuesday Night Turmoil, house shows called Live!, and an annual calendar of PPVs headed by Redemption.
promotions.history:
WPW was created by Duff, then owner of the WrestlePower.net forums, and The Judge. Its promise was that role-play quality decides results: each match had a writer who judged the two sides' RPs and wrote the match to fit, rather than results being booked for storyline reasons. Members' signups for the fed opened on 20 April 2006 (t7671).

Shows. WPW Live! opened the doors on 20 June 2006. Tuesday Night Turmoil (TNT) premiered on 4 July 2006 with The One beating Don Carlito. TNT was written by a team, with a different writer for each match and segment, plus commentary by Daniel Justice and Max Stockton, ring announcer Mina Henderson and backstage interviewer Amy White. Live! was a shorter results-style house show written by one person. After Hours (from September 2006) was Cena316's talk show, later hosted by "Tony Schiavone".

Kayfabe setting. Owner Carlos Gonzalez (Gonzales) and, later, general manager Ethan Frost ran the company. Shows toured community centres, high-school gyms and bars across Florida, Georgia, Alabama and Tennessee, and each show reported an attendance figure that rose with the number of reviews members posted.

Systems. Members earned WPW Store points by reviewing shows and spent them on Turmoil Cards, which could change a match. There were weekly rankings, momentum and popularity totals, a vBookie betting forum, WPW Fantasy, badges, and Team Warfare, where the roster was split into coloured teams scoring points for wins (season 1 MVP: The Stallion; season 2 began 25 November 2007; season 3 began at Brawl For It All 2011).

Eras. 2006 built the first champions and fought off PCW. 2007 was the Royalty vs Resistance era. 2008 brought the Hall of Fame and the dual-champion controversy. From 2009, with Mike Adams as on-screen owner, WPW ran the interactive PPV Mutiny and, in 2010, the Breakdown shows of the Coast to Coast Tour, before merging with EWE as Wrestling Evolution (see ewe).

promotions.name: E-Wrestling Evolution (EWE)
promotions.summary: Started as European Wrestling Evolution, a second fed on wrestlepower.net. In 2010 it merged with WPW to form Wrestling Evolution, and ran until its shows were cancelled in January 2012.
promotions.history:
EWE opened in November 2009 under the banner "Different Fed, Different Continent" (t16884), a European-based sister fed to WPW. Its weekly show was Awakening: Awakening 1 aired on 9 November 2009 and the numbering reached Awakening 36 on 9 January 2012. Early EWE had crowd-support scores, cash and stats, classes, "Enemies and Alliances" lists and an EWE Store.

Merger. In 2010 EWE and WPW ran a joint Draft (the "EWE/WPW Draft Special" and the "Wrestling Evolution Draft Spectacular", June 2010). According to the fan wiki the two companies merged under the E-Wrestling Evolution banner at When Worlds Collide. Titles carried over: the Florida State Championship became the United States Championship, and the fed added the Ironman Championship and the WE Tag Team titles.

Key people. "General Manager of America" Jesse Long ran the shows on screen. APostingGod ran the fed behind the scenes in 2011 and launched EWE Believe, an RPG layer where members earned points to unlock moves, crowd reactions and commentary (14 June 2011). The Wrestling Evolution Hall of Fame inducted its class of 2011, including Dan Murph.

Events found. Awakening 1–36, Damnation (12 April 2010), the Draft, Brawl For It All 2011 (Team Warfare season 3), Rebirth (2011), Cold War, a planned "South of the Border" lucha show (November 2011) and Redemption V, run in three parts from 3 to 7 December 2011. Jacob Senn won the Ironman title at Redemption V, the last time it changed hands.

End. A thread titled "All EWE show dates canceled" followed Awakening 36. In February 2012 APostingGod proposed an extended break. Instead the fed was relaunched as POWER Championship Wrestling (see pcw-power).

promotions.name: POWER Championship Wrestling (PCW)
promotions.summary: EWE relaunched under owner Ryan Blanchette as POWER Championship Wrestling, with two world titles, the Adrenaline and Live! shows and the Spring Fling and Heat Wave PPVs.
promotions.history:
PCW reused the old PCW initials and forum IDs. On screen, EWE was bought by Ryan Blanchette and turned into PCW (fan wiki, Jacob Senn page). Off screen the fed was run by APostingGod, who posted its pre-PPV questionnaires. A later thread was titled "Thank You Ryan & Jayne".

Shows. Adrenaline (Adrenaline One aired 23 March 2012) and Live! (Live! 1 on 30 March 2012), alternating weekly: "8 shows in roughly 9 weeks" by mid-May 2012. Matches were short and storyline-focused, and members were encouraged to write their own segments. PPVs: Spring Fling 2012 and Heat Wave 2012. Adrenaline 9 and later shows ran into 2013, with a preview dated 31 May 2013.

Titles. Two world titles of equal standing: the PCW World Championship (Scorch, later Justin Dreamer and El Pollo Magnifico) and the Evolution (EVO) World Championship, carried over from EWE and held by Raelis Shy. "Prestige titles" included the God of Live title, won by Mike Adams at Live! 1 by pinning Sal Karver and later held by Ammnesio, and the Savior title, held by Elijah Edwards. There were also tag team titles.

Storylines. Mike Adams vs Raelis Shy, Scorch vs 2, the Agents of Salvation (Elijah Edwards, Jacob Senn, Michael Hayden) against "POWER", the One 'N Son Connection of Ryan Blanchette and Dan Murph, D. Hero and his "true savior", Ammnesio, and Graham Stahl. A "25 Greatest of the Decade" countdown honoured WPW, EWE and PCW history.

Decline. By June 2013 Mike Adams wrote of "complete apathy". Threads asked "Still want to RP?" and announced "The Judge Retires". An offshoot, SPIRIT Pro Wrestling (2013), crowned Michael Hayden as champion before closing, and the Innovators of Wrestling forum returned to wrestlepower.net in 2013.

wrestlers.summary: WPW's first World Champion. A former actor and PCW manager who speaks in Shakespearean verse and wrestles with his mind rather than his size.
wrestlers.biography:
JMC came to WPW from PCW, where he had been a manager. He and his sister Sophie are the last of the House of Cassius and share the family castle in northern Germany. He is fiercely protective of her, and she saves him regularly.

He won the 2006 heavyweight tournament with a brass-knuckle win over Don Carlito, then beat Brock Goodman in the final at Activation with Sophie's help. His first reign lasted almost ten months and saw off Airborn, Dust, Brock Goodman, Ray Williams (steel cage), Jesse Long (ladder match, and again at Whiplash), Justin Dreamer (the first hardcore World title match) and Dan Murph (casket match). He once refereed a Goodman vs Dust match and declared himself the winner. During the PCW war he beat PCW champion The Dream by DQ.

At Redemption 2007 he lost the title to The One but sold out to owner Carlos Gonzalez to form Royalty, becoming 'the first hated-by-the-fans champion'. He won the tag titles with The Judge, then took the World title back at ToC III, briefly holding both. He held it until David Nicolls beat him at Payback 2008. Topped The List!'s Top 25 WPW Wrestlers of 2008.

In EWE he reformed Royalty with Raelis Shy, revealed as his protégé, and won the WE Tag titles with Michael Hayden. He also hosted 'JMC's Entertainment Corner' on After Hours.
wrestlers.original_signup_bio: The self-proclaimed "Prince of Cats" prizes himself on gameplans and using his mind in wrestling rather than all out attack due to his small stature. Formerly a manager, and before that an actor, he has come to WPW to gain his own personal ends, no longer in the shadow of others. His education has allowed himself to speak in a whistful, Shakespearian tone. His Family is merely his sister Sophie, who he is seen to be incredibly close to and even overprotective of, and to an extent she is overprotective of him as well. Both born into the "House of Cassius", they are now the only ones bearing the name after thier parents death and recently, thier uncle. Due to this they collectively own the family Castle in Northern Germany to which their family has ties to and have spent centuries living in. These two are no different.

wrestlers.summary: WPW's second World Champion, who headlined the first Tuesday Night Turmoil and unified the PCW and WPW titles at Redemption 2007.
wrestlers.biography:
The One headlined the first TNT on 4 July 2006, beating Don Carlito, and spent 2006 'held back' by owner Carlos Gonzalez after losing the company's sponsorships. He was never pinned or submitted in his early run, and teamed with Scorch from Full Force onward.

In March 2007 he won the PCW title in a six-man match he turned into a ladder match, then beat JMC at Redemption to unify the PCW and WPW titles, with help from 'Frankie the Forklift Driver'. He told fans for months that it was his destiny; his followers were called Believers. He lost the title at ReActivation to Scorch, one of those Believers, and led the Resistance against Royalty.

The One left WPW on 16 October 2007, losing a Tournament of Champions match to The Judge in what the writers framed as his farewell, and returned several times: tag champion with Martin Cameron in 2008, Florida State Champion at Greed 2009, and EWE tag champion with 2. In PCW 2012 he appears in the One 'N Son Connection storyline. At the 2007 awards his writer noted he was nominated for four of the five RP battles of the year.
wrestlers.original_signup_bio: The One has been wrestling for about a year now and has made quite a name for himself in PCW  now he looks to make a impact in this new upstart company. wrestlers.summary: Third WPW World Champion and creator of the weekly Scorch Open Challenge.
wrestlers.biography:
Scorch debuted at Full Force as The One's tag partner and was a key member of the Resistance. At ReActivation 2007 he beat The One for the World title, 'the third man to pass through the glass ceiling'.

As champion he ran the Scorch Open Challenge: anyone eliminated from the Tournament of Champions could face him in a non-title match, and a win earned a title shot. Gunnar Brian, Martin Cameron and Mike Corral all beat him in non-title matches and all lost the title match that followed; Martin Cameron got his after a controversial draw. Scorch lost the title without being beaten when he no-showed the ToC III PPV.

He won the second Sell Your Soul match in 2009 and the tag titles with The Judge at Fallout. In PCW 2012 he was the PCW World Champion and feuded with 2. A 2012 interview thread names his writer as Steve Dunn.

wrestlers.summary: An Irish teenager who went from WPW jobber to two-time World Champion, a defector to PCW, and the centre of WPW's biggest title controversy.
wrestlers.biography:
Murph joined PCW at 17 and won the IOW title three months after debuting. In early WPW he lost often on Live!, but the 2006 war made him: he turned on WPW, was 'everywhere' in the PCW storyline, and was among the last PCW men eliminated at When Worlds Collide. Max Stockton's line 'He's Dan Murph, BITCH!' stuck.

Back in WPW, he beat Dust and Jokester at Ruined Fate to become number one contender, lost to JMC in a casket match at Everything Ends, and held the Florida title in mid-2007. At Redemption 2008 he won the first Sell Your Soul ladder match and cashed the contract in on 15 July 2008 against new champion David Nicolls. Both men's shoulders were down; both were named champion. He lost his half to The Killing Joke on his 21st birthday at When Worlds Collide 2008.

His storyline then turned dark: rehab for alcohol, and blaming WPW for his downfall. He beat The Stallion for the title at Fallout 2009 vowing to take the company down, and claimed to be in league with owner Mike Adams after a fast-count win over Sal Karver at Mutiny. EWE held a 'Dan Murph Farewell Interview' and billed a 2011 match as his last. In PCW 2012 he teamed with Ryan Blanchette as the One 'N Son Connection.

wrestlers.biography:
Brock's signup was the first in WPW (20 April 2006). He lost the first World title tournament final to JMC at Activation, was banned from the arena for attacking JMC afterwards, and stayed in the title picture through Full Force. He teamed with Ave Cali as Beauty and the Beast.

In August 2007 his finisher For Now... Sleep broke Ben Whyndam's neck in a match and Whyndam died, a storyline that led to a tribute show in Melbourne and Carlos Gonzalez banning the move after it also broke The Outkast Kid's wrist. Brock went into the Hallowicked 2007 20-man TLC match as 'the longest running man at WPW to not win any title' and won the Florida State title. He lost it to 2 at ToC III. Number 22 on The List!'s Top 25 of 2008.

However, as soon as he stepped out of the Church a drunk driver crashed into him and shattered both of his legs. Once healed healed Brock renounced his religion and now claims that he was sent by Lucifer to follow dark order and wipe out everything that is good in wrestling.

wrestlers.summary: Undefeated through his first months in WPW, the People's King pinned the World Champion and main-evented Full Force.
wrestlers.biography:
Dust won his first eight WPW matches, including Activation, and earned a title shot by DQ over The One. He became 'The Streak Killer' by pinning champion JMC in a tag match, and claimed he was still unbeaten after JMC refereed and declared himself winner of a Dust vs Brock Goodman match. He lost the Full Force triple threat when JMC pinned him.

His streak ended in the 'biggest upset in WPW's short history' when Daisuke Ryo pinned him on Live! on 15 October 2006, after Dust did not RP. Jesse Long beat him in the November 2006 fatal four-way, a storyline in which Dust's 'Sean Reigns' personality fought for control. His writer, Peoples King, objected publicly to being called 'the People's Champ'. Number 24 on PCW's 25 Greatest of the Decade (2012).
wrestlers.original_signup_bio: Having left Ireland to pursue his lifetime dream of becoming a professional wrestler, Dust toured wrestling schools across North America, Mexico and Japan in order to learn his trade. Though a fast learner all those who trained and trained with Dust considered him to be head strong and cocky. No matter what he was taught Dust always considered his way to be the better way to go. In his early career this obviously got the young superstar into hotwater, losing him bookings, money and contacts in the wrestling world particularily in the United States and Canada. With his possibilities of bookings in North America at a minimum, Dust concentrated on making a name for himself in Mexico but primarily in Japan. While his attitude did not change Dust did collect a cult of followers for himself in Japan which was his saving grace in regards keeping bookings coming his way. With his star on the rise in Japan, Dust returned to North America as a bigger star then when he left. The Peoples King made appearences with RoH but all talks with TNA eventually ended disasterously after a couple of weeks. RoH bookings allowed Dust to split his time between Japan and North America and also gave him more booking oppertunities in Canada and the US. Finally the break Dust was looking for came when he was signed to a development deal with WWE and asigned to OVW. wrestlers.summary: One of the few WPW originals who didn't come from PCW. Became Royalty's enforcer as the Royal Knight, then returned as The Stallion to win the World title in 2009.
wrestlers.biography:
The Stallion came from Xtreme Professional Wrestling. Early on he was sent to a sexual harassment clinic for hitting on Amy White, after a segment his writer feared had turned him heel. He won the Hardcore title in the 20-man match at When Worlds Collide, scoring WPW's first points of the night, and was Team Warfare's first MVP.

At Redemption 2007 his girlfriend Super Sexy Girl pinned him for the Hardcore title, and he joined Royalty as the Royal Knight, trading the Florida title with Jamie Parker. Thrown out of Royalty, he returned as The Stallion at Brawl For It All 2008, had his leg broken by Royalty at Redemption, and came back at ReActivation.

His feud with The Killing Joke ran through late 2008 and 2009, including Killing Joke tricking him into believing he was the father of Super Sexy Girl's child. He pinned Killing Joke at Redemption III in 2009 to become World Champion and lost the title to Dan Murph at Fallout.
wrestlers.original_signup_bio: Once known as Stallion, he has been kicked around and pushed aside for years, with only a very few seeing his true potential. Fighting through the indy feds for several years, Stallion was always known as "the greatest wrestler never to win the big one". This trend continued through XPW and WPW. Even with big profile wins and endless spots, he never reached his full potential, and was never expected to win "the big one" Enter the Royal Knight

wrestlers.biography:
Jesse Long's rivalry with Justin Dreamer began in PCW and carried into WPW: a First Blood match in September 2006 and a win over Dreamer at Full Force. On 14 November 2006 he won a fatal four-way over Ray Williams, Justin Dreamer and Dust. His RPs beat Peoples King's, which forced The Judge to rethink his Whiplash plans, and he challenged JMC there and lost. He had earlier lost a ladder match to JMC at his old high school.

In 2007 he held the God of Live title and called himself 'The Real God of Live'. In EWE and PCW 2012 he was the on-screen General Manager of America, announcing the 'South of the Border' lucha PPV in November 2011. Number 19 on PCW's 25 Greatest of the Decade.

After coming up short, Jesse’s career began to nosedive. After winning his retirement match against Kayne Risen at When Worlds Collide, Jesse began to seek out a normal life. Yeah, didn’t work out so hot. After unsuccessfully attempting to become a pixel pusher, Jesse’s life hit its low point, he started attending TNA Impact! tapings. It was there that he was found by former PCW Champion Masterful Michael Karver. Now under the tutelage of MMK, Jesse looks to regain the glory that he once had years ago.

wrestlers.biography:
Dreamer forced his way into the Activation Florida match by chair-shotting MVP and The Stallion. He fought Jesse Long repeatedly, got a standing ovation after losing the first hardcore World title match to JMC on Halloween 2006, and turned on Ben Whyndam with a chair during the Whiplash tag gauntlet.

In 2007 he beat The Stallion twice for the Hardcore title, pinned Phill Bennett to become God of Live and 'WPW's first God of Hardcore', and later lost the title to Martin Cameron, who injured him. He was revealed as the SAW 'Puppet' stalking Carlos Gonzalez at Hallowicked 2007 and joined the Resistance. A later team with Mike Corral, Extreme Airborne, ended against IOW, and Dreamer vanished for two years.

He returned to beat The Judge at Mutiny 2009 and rename the Canadian title the Pure Championship. In PCW 2012 he beat Michael Hayden on Adrenaline 4 and became PCW Champion. Number 21 on the 25 Greatest of the Decade.

With Jake constantly moaning on about his career in wrestling and showing wrestling videos non stop, Jamie caught the bug and when he was discharged he enlisted in a wrestling school. Later he formed Extreme Airborne with Justin Dreamer.

As Michael Hayden he joined EWE, won the WE Tag titles with JMC at Rebirth, lost to Raelis Shy at When Worlds Collide 2011 without ever striking her, and beat Dan Murph in 'Dan Murph's last match'. In PCW 2012 he joined the Agents of Salvation and finally beat The Judge at Spring Fling. Number 25 on PCW's 25 Greatest of the Decade.

After one particularly vicious night, Matthew decided that enough was enough and attacked his father. Breaking his nose and nearly knocking him unconsciouss, Matthew left his house, going to Marilyn's house to ask her to run away with him. Unfortunately, he came just as Brandon was leaving. Matthew had nothing to lose, so attacked him as well in the front yard, beating him with anything he could get his hands on before leaving. After getting towards Albany, he called an uncle who lived in New Jersey and asked to live with him. Spending three years there, Matthew found solace and discovered a passion for fighting, joining a gang. As his uncle saw this, he realized that Matthew had potential and gave him the number to a wrestling school that was nearby. Afer 6 months, Matthew graduated at the top of his class and joined an upstart wrestling fed called New Jersey Pro Wrestling. After months of build-up, Matthew (now called Twizted) debuted at the first PPV, "The Very Best", competing in a tournament to determine the Heavyweight Champion. Making it to the end, Twizted lost the final match but won the attention and respect of the crowd and the wrestlers. The two instantly fell in love. After winning many contests, Seto realized his dream of going to America and was quickly disappointed to find out martial arts wasn't as popular in this country. With only a name for a friend, Seto traveled to Atlanta where he met Vendetta instead of the man he was supposed to meet (Nigel McGuinnes). stables.name: Royalty
stables.members: James Moriarty Cassius, The Judge, The Royal Knight, 2; backed by owner Carlos Gonzalez. Re-formed in EWE with Raelis Shy.
stables.history: Formed at Redemption 2007 when JMC sold out to Carlos Gonzalez during his title loss to The One. Royalty's tactics were 'about planning, not rushing in'. They held the tag titles from ReActivation 2007 to January 2008, had three members in the 2007 Tournament of Champions, and won all three titles at once when 2 joined at ToC III. Royalty fell apart after D&D took the tag titles under a stipulation that the losing team would split. The Judge and JMC re-formed it in EWE with Raelis Shy.

feuds.name: JMC vs Brock Goodman vs Dust
feuds.story: The first main-event story. Brock lost the tournament final to JMC at Activation, attacked him, and was banned from the arena. Dust, unbeaten, earned a shot by DQ over The One and pinned JMC in a tag match. JMC refereed Goodman vs Dust and declared himself the winner, then the Cassius siblings lost to Goodman and Dust. It ended in the Full Force triple threat, where JMC pinned Dust after Boris interfered and Sophie went after Goodman.

feuds.name: MVP vs Nick Comoroto
feuds.story: Comoroto won a four-way to become number one contender, took the title from MVP in a bloody hardcore match at Full Force, and 'purified' it. MVP's rematches failed: he tapped to the Border City Stretch when Harry Allanson distracted the referee, then won only by countout at Whiplash. Comoroto finally lost to Mykal Adams.

feuds.name: The WPW–PCW War
feuds.story: Rumours that WPW was trying to put PCW out of business turned into a storyline. PCW Champion Mike Adams showed up on TNT, Team PCW beat Team WPW at Whiplash, Mike Corral betrayed Dust and The Stallion, and Dan Murph defected. The 12 and 19 December TNTs ran PCW matches, including PCW title changes, inside WPW's show. Carlos Gonzalez recruited protection and accused PCW of 'cheap tactics to steal talent'. When Worlds Collide on 3 January 2007 settled it: WPW won the five-on-five main event and PCW closed. The Judge's note on the last TNT of 2006 said that, depending on the result, it might be the last TNT ever.

feuds.name: Royalty vs The Resistance
feuds.story: WPW's defining 2007 story. Royalty, the owner's chosen faction, against the faces led by The One and Scorch. It covered the World title (Scorch's Open Challenges while Royalty plotted an ambush), the tag titles, Justin Dreamer's return as the 'Puppet', and the Tournament of Champions, which Royalty dominated.

feuds.name: Royalty vs D&D
feuds.story: A series of 'Royalty vs D&D challenges' on Live! with novelty stipulations ('Half Price Hot Dogs', 'Buy Two DVDs Get A Working One Free'). It continued through a two-out-of-three-falls title match at Hallowicked and ToC matches, and ended when D&D won the tag titles under a stipulation that the losing team would split.

feuds.name: Dan Murph vs David Nicolls
feuds.story: Murph cashed in his Sell Your Soul contract two weeks after Nicolls won the title. Both men's shoulders were down for the count, and the 'EXTREMELY controversial decision' named both champion. Each carried a belt, and ReActivation 2008 had two World title matches: Scorch vs Murph and Killing Joke vs Nicolls. Killing Joke ended it by beating both.

feuds.name: The Stallion vs The Killing Joke
feuds.story: The Stallion became number one contender at When Worlds Collide 2008. Killing Joke tricked him into believing he had fathered Super Sexy Girl's child. Stallion beat Killing Joke by countout at Brawl For It All 2009, which left KJ with the title, then forced his way into the Redemption III main event and pinned Killing Joke for the title.

feuds.name: Gunnar Brian vs Sal Karver
feuds.story: A bloody feud over the Florida title: Karver won it at When Worlds Collide, Gunnar took it back in a Five Floors of Hell match, Karver won a weapons-only-for-him match and then lost a cage match at Brawl For It All when he threw Gunnar through the door, and finally won it back in April 2009.

feuds.name: Mike Adams vs Raelis Shy
feuds.story: The headline PCW 2012 story, built across Adrenaline and Live!. Several members called it their favourite storyline in the May 2012 questionnaire.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The Live! RP rule and the favouritism row
storylines_and_controversies.story: WPW's rule was that if you didn't RP, you could lose to anyone. On Live! the writer flipped a coin when neither side RPed. Members argued over it repeatedly. Cena316 objected in August 2006 to jokes about non-RPers. In October, Ncomo lost to jobbers Red Rover without RPing and accused Live! writer Mike Adams of favouritism. The Judge, Duff, Philly, Gravity and Cena316 replied that Dust and Jesse Long had also lost to jobbers for not RPing. Duff thanked Mike Adams publicly in November 2006 for being the only person to RP for a whole Live!.

storylines_and_controversies.name: SiNN's joke Live!
storylines_and_controversies.story: AFS (SiNN) wrote the 23 September 2006 Live! as a comedy show because almost nobody had RPed, including a match won by 'the Baker man'. The Judge said publicly he disagreed '100%' despite being his friend, comparing it to how PCW's Live! had been ruined. Chazz and Cena316 came round to that view, and AFS agreed to limit the humour to one match in future.

storylines_and_controversies.name: Real wrestling personalities in After Hours
storylines_and_controversies.story: Cena316 'hired' Tony Schiavone as host of After Hours. Scorch criticised using real personalities as lazy and pointed out a recap error. Cena replied that an invented host would be 'just another nobody'.

storylines_and_controversies.name: Writing other people's characters
storylines_and_controversies.story: Recurring arguments about segments written by someone other than the character's player. HBK619 felt a segment had turned The Stallion heel (July 2006). Peoples King said a backstage segment before Full Force was 'un-Dust like'. Mike Corral thanked the writer who made Corral 'an asshole with a God complex, yet still somehow a face'. In 2012, PCW members asked to write their own segments for this reason.

storylines_and_controversies.name: Is Jamie Parker a two-time tag champion?
storylines_and_controversies.story: Duff asked why Jamie Parker counted as a two-time tag champion when he had never lost the belts. The Judge ruled that titles are won and lost as a team, so 'Parker and Maddox' and 'Parker and Bennett' are separate reigns. Aperama later asked whether Forsaken's quick title changes during the ReActivation scramble counted.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The Scorch vs Martin Cameron draw
storylines_and_controversies.story: Snowman, Martin Cameron's writer, protested that he had not earned the draw with Scorch that gave him a title shot. Match writer Chazz replied that he and The Judge judged the RPs close, and that Snowman's own post 'made it look like' his effort was less than average.

storylines_and_controversies.name: Does the World title always main-event?
storylines_and_controversies.story: Aperama argued that Scorch's weekly title matches always closing TNT left hotter feuds underneath. The Judge replied that real bad booking would be hiding the champion for three months during a 32-man tournament.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The 'Soon...' mystery
storylines_and_controversies.story: Who first used 'Soon...' as a teaser? M Karver (Ric Susman) claimed it, APostingGod claimed the orange rhyming version, Duff said neither was first and that a storyline had been running unnoticed, and AFS credited The Judge. The Judge said 'Correct.'

storylines_and_controversies.name: Trent James vs WPW Management
storylines_and_controversies.story: A dispute played out in press releases. WPW Management said Trent James had complained about never getting a proper push, despite being in more number one contender matches than anyone and being placed in the Sell Your Soul match. Trent replied that management kept rejecting his ideas. He left for EWE while still Florida Champion.

storylines_and_controversies.name: Two World Champions
storylines_and_controversies.story: The 15 July 2008 double pin between Dan Murph and David Nicolls was billed as an 'EXTREMELY controversial decision'. WPW recognised two World Champions until ReActivation. See feud-dual-champions.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The death of Ben Whyndam
storylines_and_controversies.story: Brock Goodman botched For Now... Sleep and Ben Whyndam 'suffered a broken neck' and died, aged 21. The next show paused all storylines for a tribute in Melbourne with the original tag champions, ending with Goodman unable to speak. WPW later said Whyndam's family declined a Hall of Fame induction because of an 'unpublicized legal battle'.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The Tank / El Pollo / KFC incident
storylines_and_controversies.story: A spoof news report by Tank2K8: Tank attacked at a KFC, Al Sharpton leading a protest, Jokester confronting him, and El Pollo Negro attacking police with his 'Chicken Dog Hybrid'. Some members loved it; it was edgy enough that it is recorded here as a controversy.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The Billy James name change
storylines_and_controversies.story: After losing a loser-changes-name match, APostingGod's 'Good Ole' Billy James (by then James Montel Cookiemonster) tried to take the name Billy James back, clashing with the other Billy James. Moderator AFS ruled he had lost the right to it. Duff argued the stipulation never barred changing it back. He settled on Billy Montel.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The Mutiny fast count
storylines_and_controversies.story: Dan Murph beat Sal Karver for the World title with a fast count, supporting Murph's claim that he was in league with owner Mike Adams. Karver attacked the referee.

storylines_and_controversies.name: The end of the feds
storylines_and_controversies.story: After EWE's show dates were cancelled in January 2012, APostingGod said he had 'zero want' to write shows nobody read and proposed a three-month break. PCW relaunched in March 2012, but by June 2013 Mike Adams answered APostingGod's offer to take over with 'you taking over isn't going to fix the complete apathy'. Michael Hayden's writer replied, 'YOU ALL STILL HAVE HAYDEN!'
